brief: Three matching attic paintings lit by Vale's off-camera held lantern, with no painted lantern or lamp. Lit is a warm refuge with an ordinary attic reflection. Lit with the scarf reveals the descent into Cosy Cottage while retaining that reflection. Only the doused state reveals the moonlit Black Pond through the mirror.
art_direction_feedback: Preserve the same camera, perspective, rafters, stair opening and balustrade, shrouded furniture, trunks, city windows, ornate mirror and painterly style for crossfades.
Remove the standing floor lamp entirely and restore bare boards at its old position.
Keep the lower-left foreground as clear, uncluttered floorboards for Vale.
In lit states, warm amber light originates outside the picture, just in front of and below the camera, slightly left of centre. The near floor and trunk fronts receive the brightest light.
Both lit states show only an ordinary warm reflection of the attic; no Black Pond or visible figure in the mirror.
Only the doused state shows the Black Pond, the brightest area in the cold blue-black room, with a thin curl of smoke entering from the lower left.
In the cottage state, a long soft heather knitted scarf marks the balustrade above a clear descent into a blue timber cottage with kettle, basket and softer hearth firelight.
No people, visible lanterns, lamps, candles, light fixtures or text in any delivered painting.
